metadata.title: When History Misleads
metadata.audience: Students learning how reinforcement learning agents can be misled by their inputs
metadata.greeting_note: HAI short-form hello lexicon: Norwegian 'Hei' (not used by the earlier reels: Hej, Ciao, Ola, Hallo). The greeting addresses the person typing (Laksh).
metadata.source_commit_subject: Add Huawei multi-week traces and a PPO agent that sets HPA's target
metadata.evidence: evidence/make_evidence.py (run in the rl-autoscaler venv) -> evidence/evidence.json, embedded in scenes.py
metadata.brutalist_checked: 2026-11-22 (same toolkit commit as the earlier videos)
metadata.ai_disclosure: Narration is an AI voice (Kokoro af_bella). The project is Laksh's work, built with help from Claude Code. Beat sheet, scenes and renders were produced by Claude Code from the repo's code and results.

render.note: 4K-native sources: Manim at 2160p24, Remotion at scale 2.

metadata.note: STEM explainer on the claude-hai channel: an RL autoscaler misled by wrong history, and training with misleading history (domain randomization). No week numbers. Every number comes from evidence/evidence.json.
metadata.source_data: Azure Functions Trace 2019 (Shahrad et al., USENIX ATC 2020), CC-BY 4.0; Huawei Cloud traces 2023 (Joosen et al., ACM SoCC 2023), CC BY 4.0

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW: composer, the ask lands answered. Required fellows intro line first, then the AI-voice disclosure.
beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Laksh, and this video is about what happens when an AI autoscaler trusts history that is wrong. The voice is an AI voice; the project is my own work, built with help from Claude Code.
beats.new_visual_element: Claude composer: the ask and three results

show.event: greeting and the ask type into the composer
running indicator, then three result lines land

props.command: replay every test day with a wrong yesterday or last week, and compare the agent with HPA
output: normal training: beats HPA in 208 of 360

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW: the hesitant writer types the default (clean history) and corrects it (misleading history).
beats.narration_text: An autoscaler that plans from yesterday can be fooled when yesterday was unusual. The fix: train it on misleading history, on purpose.

show.event: the writer types 'Train the agent on clean history.'
'clean' turns terracotta, is deleted, 'misleading' is typed

props.text:
Train the agent
on clean history.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the overview is typed token by token, so mid-beat frames are mostly cream by design.

beats.qc_note: Portrait only: fontSize 160 (landscape 120) so the lowercase runs clear GATE T's 72 px floor at 3840.

beats.role_note: HPA's target set by PPO each minute (train.py Headroom, HEADROOM_TARGETS) and the 35-number observation (env.py _obs, WEEKLY config)
beats.narration_text: The Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, or HPA, adds servers as load rises. A reinforcement learning agent sets its target every minute, and sees the past only as slices of yesterday's and last week's traffic.
beats.new_visual_element: a target slider 40-90% that PPO moves; then the 35 numbers as four rows of cells

show.event: HPA chip; target slider 40% to 90%
the PPO marker moves along the slider, minute by minute
35 cells grow in by group: last 10 minutes, yesterday next 10, last week next 10, 5 others
the yesterday and last-week rows get a gold outline: its only view of the past

beats.role_note: a real Azure test day (evidence example) and stress.py's three changes
beats.narration_text: Normally that helps: yesterday's burst came at the same minute, so the agent can ready servers, which take three minutes to boot. But yesterday may have been a holiday, a launch, or a metrics outage.
beats.new_visual_element: today and yesterday on one real day; yesterday morphs to x0.2, x3, x0

show.event: today (navy) and yesterday (teal) lines, the same-minute burst
a 3-minute boot bracket before the burst
yesterday shrinks to 20% (holiday)
the axis zooms out, yesterday is 3x (launch)
yesterday is all zero (metrics outage)
HPA chip: plans from no history

beats.role_note: results/stress-hpa.json, normal-trained agent vs HPA at equal cost
beats.narration_text: I replayed every test day with history changed like this, against HPA at the same cost. Trained on normal history, the agent wins fifty-eight percent of cases; at worst, it has ninety-three percent more late requests.
beats.new_visual_element: 360 squares: 6 changes x 4 test sets x 15 runs; better cases fill teal

show.event: 6 blocks of 60 squares grow in, one block per change
same-cost note
the cases where the agent beats HPA fill teal; per-block counts; 208 of 360
worst case: +93% late requests

beats.narration_text: The fix: in thirty percent of training episodes, scale yesterday or last week at random, or zero it. This is domain randomization: randomize what can go wrong, so the policy does not depend on it.
beats.new_visual_element: 10 training episodes, 3 changed; a number line 0.1x to 5x plus 0 with real draws

show.event: 10 episode tiles grow in; 3 get a gold outline and their factor
number line 0.1x to 5x, and 0; 40 draws drop onto it
domain randomization label

beats.role_note: results/stress-hpa.json, misleading-trained agent vs normal-trained agent
beats.narration_text: Now it wins seventy-six percent, and its worst case drops to sixty-four percent. On normal history it is no worse: fifty-five of sixty runs beat HPA, against fifty-three.
beats.new_visual_element: the same 360 squares, now the misleading-trained agent; counts and normal history

show.event: the 360 squares as in B04
squares refill for the misleading-trained agent; 273 of 360
worst case 93% to 64%
normal history: 53 vs 55 of 60 bars

beats.role_note: README Limits; stress.py change sizes vs real_traffic range
beats.narration_text: A caution: tests and training used the same kinds of change. Real irregular days, like a recorded outage in public web server logs, are the stronger test, and come next. HPA is never fooled by history; the agent sometimes is.
beats.new_visual_element: training range 0.1x-5x plus 0 as an outlined bracket; test sizes land inside; next step chip

show.event: training range bracket grows
test changes 0.2x, 3x, 0 drop inside it
next: real irregular days chip
HPA never fooled / agent sometimes

beats.role_note: recap card; the narration carries the takeaway
beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. If your model reads history, assume it can be wrong, and train on wrong history too.

show.event: the artifact card lists five lines

artifactLines: The agent's only past: slices of yesterday and last week.
Wrong history, normal training: beats HPA in 58%.
Worst case: 93% more late requests, now 64%.
Normal history: 55 of 60 runs better, was 53.

beats.role_note: YOUR TURN LAW: one prompt the viewer can paste, read aloud and discussed
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude. Here are the inputs my model reads about the past. List three ways they could be wrong, and write a training step that applies them at random. Compare its list with failures you have seen.
